comments.content: The decrement `idle_threads--` here in `tryWakeUpAnyOtherThreadWithTasks` is only executed on the code path that pops a thread from `threads_queue`. Please verify that every branch that removes a thread from `threads_queue` (including the branch selecting a specific thread vs. `popAny()`) is covered, and that `idle_threads` cannot go negative if a thread is woken up but was not counted as idle. Since `idle_threads` is `std::atomic_size_t`, an underflow would wrap to a huge value and make `shouldSpawn()` permanently return false, effectively stalling thread spawning for the query.

`idle_threads` is a `std::atomic_size_t` but the increments/decrements in ExecutorTasks.cpp all happen under the tasks mutex (same lock guarding `threads_queue`). If it is always mutated under the lock, an atomic is unnecessary; if it is intended to be read via `shouldSpawn()` without the lock, then the increment/decrement/read sequences are not consistent (e.g. push+increment vs. the read in shouldSpawn can race). Clarify the intended synchronization: either keep it under the lock as a plain size_t, or ensure all mutations are lock-free-safe. As written, `shouldSpawn()` reads without the lock while other threads mutate, which is fine for atomics but the value can be stale/inconsistent with `threads_queue.size()`.

With the `try_to_lock` short-circuit, if thread A holds `spawn_lock` and is mid-spawn while thread B calls `spawnThreads()` and returns early, there is a risk that newly-arrived tasks needing more threads never trigger another spawn. Confirm that `spawnThreads()` is re-invoked after tasks are pushed (e.g. on every wakeup / task enqueue) so that a skipped spawn attempt is eventually retried; otherwise the pipeline could under-spawn and stall when `shouldSpawn()` briefly returned false or the lock was contended.
